# Syntropy Earth

> Social impact and CSR programme design for organisations already carrying an obligation: a Section 135 CSR mandate, a head-office commitment, a duty-of-care exposure or a BRSR assurance deadline. A brand and growth consultancy practice sits alongside it. Based in Bengaluru, India.

Syntropy Earth is a founder-led advisory practice run by Abhijith Magal, who spent nine years across two global pharmaceutical multinationals before founding it, including brand and commercial work across more than 40 countries, a landmark obesity treatment launch, and health-equity and social responsibility leadership working directly with the WHO-Foundation and UNICEF.

The governing idea is that climate change reaches people first as a health and access problem rather than an environmental one. The sharper operating statement is the completion spine: closing the gap between an entitlement existing and a person actually receiving it. Work attaches to a budget that is already moving rather than to a category, which means mandated CSR spend under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, headquarters duty-of-care mandates, employer duty of care to a workforce, or a BRSR assurance clock.

## The two practices

**Social Impact.** The flagship. CSR programme design under Section 135, health equity and patient access programme design, workforce heat and duty of care, and BRSR assurance readiness. Programmes are built around the company's own mission and designed to survive a board question, an auditor and a change of CSR head. Work usually starts by reading the existing portfolio, because valuable activity is normally already being undercounted or tagged against the wrong goal. Measurement maps to BRSR and GRI. Implementing-partner screening runs to a published standard, and Syntropy Earth takes no money from implementing partners in any form. Design comes first, with implementation and handover behind it.

**Brand and Growth.** Marketing and management consultancy built on nine years of commercial work across global markets. Brand strategy and full brand plans, launch packs from ideation through sales-force effectiveness, operational improvement, cost and financial models, capability centre build-out, and agency orchestration. Priced and delivered as strategy, with an execution partner brought in transparently where execution is required.

**Climate Access Stress Test (CAST).** The scored diagnostic that sits under the social impact practice. Four dimensions, four seasons, one score: geographic exposure, supply chain and operational continuity, workforce availability, and financial and demand continuity, each read across heat, monsoon, air and drought. Includes pathway analysis of how one break cascades into others, and produces disclosure-ready climate-access metrics. CAVS-S is its free, self-serve, directional version.

Explicitly not offered, and referred out: technical ESG, net-zero roadmapping, emissions accounting, and disclosure assurance.

## Thinking (articles)

- [Thinking index](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/): Evidence-led writing on where climate change meets healthcare.
- [Implementing Partner Screening: IPSS v1.0](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/implementing-partner-screening/): The Implementation Partner Screening Standard, a published method for choosing between eligible CSR implementing organisations under Section 135, with DOIs for the standard (10.5281/zenodo.22814160) and white paper (10.5281/zenodo.22823149).
- [Climate Change Is a Healthcare Story](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/climate-change-is-a-healthcare-story/): The core argument for reading climate as a health and access problem first.
- [Why the Heat Season Is a Healthcare Operations Problem](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/india-heat-season-healthcare-operations/): Extreme heat as a workforce, access and supply-chain problem, not just a medical one.
- [The Climate Risk Hiding in Your Access Data](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/climate-risk-hiding-in-your-access-data/): How seasonal signals of climate disruption already sit in programme data nobody has read that way.
- [The Lancet Countdown 2025, in India's Operating Terms](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/lancet-countdown-2025-india-operating-terms/): What the 2025 findings mean for organisations operating in India.
- [When the HQ Climate-Health Mandate Lands on the India Arm](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/hq-climate-health-mandate-india-arm/): What to do when a global headquarters commitment arrives with a deadline attached.

- [COP History & Global Climate Targets](https://syntropyearth.com/guide/frameworks/cop.html): What each commitment actually binds a country to.
